sections.h2: How can a Clay homeowner sell, and which route fits?
sections.html:
A Clay homeowner has three realistic routes: an agent listing, a sale without an agent, or an as-is purchase for cash. The right route depends on how much time you have, what shape the house is in and whether you can carry the mortgage and taxes while you wait for a buyer.

A traditional listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers, but it asks you to prepare the house, allow showings and accept financing contingencies. A cash buyer removes most of that. The trade-off is that a cash offer sits below what a fully prepared listing might reach, so compare the net figure from each route after taxes, liens and closing costs.

  • Hire an agent if the house shows well and you are comfortable waiting out weekend open houses.
  • Sell by owner when you already have a buyer or want to avoid a commission and can handle the paperwork.
  • Take a cash offer when the house needs work, tenants are in place, the estate is unsettled or you need a fixed closing date.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the town of Clay itself?
sections.html:
Clay is the largest town in Onondaga County and sits directly north of Syracuse. The Oneida River forms the northern boundary with Oswego County and the Seneca River marks the western line. Most of the shopping sits along NY Route 31, with NY Route 481 crossing it near Euclid. The town was formed in 1827 out of Cicero and was named for Henry Clay.

Housing is mostly suburban. Named subdivisions such as Fairway East, Lawton Valley Hunt, Country Meadow and The Farmstead sit beside older hamlets like Euclid, Moyers Corners, Belgium and Three Rivers. In October 2022 Micron Technology announced a semiconductor complex at the White Pine Commerce Park in Clay, which has kept the town in regional news ever since.

The Census Bureau counted 60,527 residents in 2020 and estimates 59,285 for July 1, 2025. The table below shows the housing and income picture that matters when you price a sale.

sections.h2: Which school districts and neighborhoods affect a sale in Clay?
sections.html:
Clay is split among five school districts, and the district printed on a tax bill often shapes how buyers read a listing. The Town Tax Receiver says the two largest are Liverpool and North Syracuse, with smaller portions in Baldwinsville, Phoenix and Central Square.

That split also changes the bill. The assessor's tax page lists school rates per thousand dollars of full market value that range from $18.58 for Central Square to $28.21 for Liverpool, with North Syracuse at $23.22. Onondaga County is listed at $5.14 per thousand, and the Town levies are $1.94 for highway, $0.96 for fire protection and $0.75 for administration. A separate county sewer charge of $417.07 per residential unit appears on the same page. Ask the assessor which year those rates describe before you quote them to a buyer.

Fire protection comes from five volunteer fire departments under contract with the Town, and the Town's Water Department serves its own district. A buyer will look at all of these lines, so having a recent bill in hand helps.

sections.h2: What does the Clay tax calendar mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Clay residents pay Town and County taxes in January, school taxes in the fall and, inside the Village of North Syracuse, a village bill in the summer. The Tax Receiver's office collects all of them for any parcel wholly or partly inside the Town.

  • Town and County bills are mailed around January 1 and are due without penalty by January 31.
  • School bills are mailed around September 1 and are due without penalty around October 1.
  • North Syracuse village bills are mailed around June 1 and are due without penalty July 1.
  • The office also processes payments for the one water district the Town runs.

Payments can be made online through the Onondaga County Department of Finance, by mailed check or in the drop box in front of Town Hall at 4401 State Route 31. At a closing, the title company normally prorates these bills between buyer and seller, so request paid receipts and any open balance ahead of time. Ask the Tax Receiver for current balances rather than relying on an old bill.

sections.h2: How do assessments and grievances work in Clay?
sections.html:
The Clay assessor works from a calendar set by state law. March 1 is both the taxable status date and the deadline for every exemption application, and the Town says there are no exceptions. The tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May, and the final roll is filed July 1.

Grievance Day in 2026 was May 26, with the Board of Assessment Review sitting from 4 to 8 p.m. at Town Hall, so that window has closed. The next one falls on the fourth Tuesday in May 2027. After Grievance Day nothing on the roll can change until the next taxable status year, and those values feed the September school bill and the January Town and County bill. The Town posts a grievance form online, along with instructions for filing an appeal.

If you are about to sell, a late grievance will not help you, but the roll still matters: it tells a buyer's lender what the taxable value is. Exemptions the assessor processes include veterans, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and limited incomes, agricultural assessment, clergy, nonprofit and commercial or industrial exemptions. Basic STAR is registered with New York State, not the Town.

sections.h2: What local offices handle permits, deeds and utilities in Clay?
sections.html:
Start with the Town departments directory, which lists the assessor, code enforcement, planning and development, the highway department, the Tax Receiver, the Town Clerk and the water department. Code enforcement handles building permits, inspections and zoning compliance, which matters if you finished a basement or added a deck without a permit.

Deeds are recorded by the Onondaga County Clerk, not by the Town. State transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of consideration, the seller normally pays it, and Form TP-584 goes to the county clerk with the deed within 15 days of delivery. Ask the clerk what the current recording charges are. The Town Clerk keeps Town records and acts as a licensing agent. Before closing, confirm that any open permits are closed out and that no unpaid water or sewer charges remain on the parcel.

faqs.q: Does a Clay house with deferred repairs still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. An as-is sale does not require repairs, though the price reflects the work a buyer takes on. Before you accept, get the code enforcement office to confirm there are no open permits or violations, since those can slow any closing.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax if I own a house in Clay?
faqs.a: The Clay Tax Receiver collects Town, County, school and North Syracuse village taxes for parcels inside the Town. Town and County bills are due January 31, and school bills are due around October 1.

faqs.q: Is Grievance Day still open in Clay this year?
faqs.a: No. Grievance Day for 2026 was May 26, so the window is closed. The next one is the fourth Tuesday in May 2027, and exemption applications for that year are due March 1.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Clay house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. Five districts reach into Clay: Liverpool, North Syracuse, Baldwinsville, Phoenix and Central Square. The district name appears on the school tax bill, and the Tax Receiver can confirm it.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Clay property?
faqs.a: At the Onondaga County Clerk, since a deed is filed with the clerk for the county that holds the land. Contact that office for current forms and fees before you schedule a closing.
